definitions.name: Calendar-varying finite-memory RIPW class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)=\{(P,\Pi,\mu,m,\tau):\Pi_s\ge\epsilon,\ \pi_s(X)\ge c_{\pi},\ Y_t=Y_t(W),\ \mathbb E_P[Y_t(s)\mid W=s,X]=\mu_t(s,X),\ \mu_t(s,X)=m_t(X)+\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\tau_{t,\ell}(X)(D_s)_{t,\ell},\ G(\Pi)\succ0\ \text{for all }s\in\mathcal S,\ t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\}\).

definitions.name: Lag-design matrices
definitions.construction: For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), set \((D_s)_{t,j}=s_{t-j}\) for \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), using \(s_u=0\) for \(u\le0\).

definitions.name: Reshaped fixed-effect coefficient
definitions.construction: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), set \(A_s(\Pi)=T^{-1}G(\Pi)^{-1}R_s(\Pi)^{\top}\), and set \(\theta(\Pi)=\mathbb E_P[\{\Pi_W/\pi_W(X)\}A_W(\Pi)Y]\).

definitions.name: Ordered Green kernel
definitions.construction: Order \(\mathcal S\) by \(a(s)\), define \(F_{\Pi}(u)=\sum_s\Pi_s\mathbf 1\{a(s)\le u\}\), and set \(K_{\Pi}(u,v)=F_{\Pi}(\min\{u,v\})-F_{\Pi}(u)F_{\Pi}(v)\).

definitions.name: Ordered pair contributions
definitions.construction: For ordered paths \(s_a,s_b\) with \(1\le a<b\le k\), \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), set \(E_{ab}=D_{s_a}-D_{s_b}\), \(B_{ab}=T^{-1}E_{ab}^{\top}JE_{ab}\), \(b_{ab,t,\ell}=T^{-1}E_{ab}^{\top}Je_t(E_{ab})_{t,\ell}\), and \(H_{\mathcal S}=\sum_{1\le a<b\le k}B_{ab}\).

definitions.name: Ordered Green sign handle
definitions.construction: Apply the adjacent-mass \(LDL^{\top}\) factorization of the bridge kernel \(K_{\Pi}\), followed by Cauchy--Binet expansions of the minors of \(G(\Pi)\) and the numerators \(h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\), to derive a sign-and-zero rule for the entries of \(L(\Pi)\).

statements.statement: For every positive reshaping law \(\Pi\), \(G(\Pi)=\sum_{a<b}\Pi_{s_a}\Pi_{s_b}B_{ab}\), \(h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)=\sum_{a<b}\Pi_{s_a}\Pi_{s_b}b_{ab,t,\ell}\), and \(\ker G(\Pi)=\bigcap_{a<b}\ker(JE_{ab})=\ker H_{\mathcal S}\). Hence nonsingularity is a support-only property and holds for one positive law if and only if it holds for every positive law on \(\mathcal S\).
statements.justification: This identity separates support identification from the numerical choice of positive reshaping probabilities.
statements.gap: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo impose positive definiteness for their dynamic regression but do not give this support-only ordered pair characterization.
statements.consumer: The public \(\texttt{ripw}\) workflow can reject an underidentified lag specification before fitting an assignment model.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\), the reshaped fixed-effect coefficient satisfies \(\theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}\). Moreover, for \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), \(G_{jr}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}K_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)-T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}K_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r)\), \(h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\{K_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)-T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}K_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\}\), and \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag causal map required to interpret a distributed-lag fixed-effect regression under a reshaped path law.
statements.gap: The closest published RIPW result gives lag coefficients only under calendar-homogeneous effects, while Sun and Abraham's decomposition concerns conventional event-time regressors rather than a reshaped finite-memory lag design.
statements.consumer: The OpenTable state-of-emergency analysis can report the precise calendar dates and causal lags contributing to each current or lag coefficient.

statements.statement: If \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\tau_{r,\ell}\) for every \(t,r\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), then \(\theta_j(\Pi)=\tau_{t,j}\) for every \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and every legal \(t\), reproducing Theorem \(4.1\) of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo. The extension is strict: for \(T=3\), \(p=1\), \(\mathcal S=\{000,001,011\}\), and \(\Pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), the calendar-varying model yields \(\theta_0=(\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2\) and \(\theta_1=(-\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2+\tau_{3,1}\), so the coefficient vector is not determined by a time-homogeneous lag-effect vector outside the comparator's submodel.
statements.justification: The reduction anchors the tensor to the published dynamic RIPW theorem while the three-period witness proves that retaining calendar time adds genuine identifying content.
statements.gap: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo and de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille both impose time-constant distributed-lag effects for their coefficient recovery results.
statements.consumer: Applied users can distinguish a valid homogeneous dynamic interpretation from calendar-specific current-effect contamination rather than silently pooling the two.

statements.statement: For integer \(T,p\), an explicitly listed binary support \(\mathcal S\), and rational \(\epsilon,\Pi,\omega\), there is a terminating exact rational-arithmetic procedure that returns either a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb Q^{d}\) with \(JE_{ab}v=0\) for every \(a<b\), certifying singularity, or the exact tensor \(L(\Pi)\), the exact value \(\mathcal C(\Pi,Q)\), and the complete sign-and-zero table of \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)-Q_{j,t,\ell}\).
statements.justification: The population theorem becomes an auditable diagnostic rather than a numerical auxiliary regression with hidden tolerance choices.
statements.gap: Existing event-study weight diagnostics compute realized-design weights numerically; they do not provide exact rational certificates for a counterfactual reshaping law and a calendar-by-causal-lag target.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{ripw}\) package can export a machine-checkable loading table for each OpenTable specification.

statements.statement: For arbitrary ordered absorbing support \(\mathcal S\) and positive law \(\Pi\), derive a necessary-and-sufficient rule, expressed only through adjacent adoption-mass ratios and ordered interval endpoints, for the sign and vanishing of every \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)\); in particular, characterize exactly when all off-diagonal causal-lag loadings vanish. The construction must cover repeated boundary cumulative coordinates and every nonsingular support-rank stratum.
statements.justification: A closed sign law is the genuinely open structural content beyond computing the tensor at one supplied law.
statements.gap: Sun and Abraham and Wright diagnose cross-horizon contamination from residualized event-time regressors, but no adjacent-mass sign frontier is available for reshaped finite-memory carryover coefficients.
statements.consumer: The diagnostic would tell an OpenTable analyst which calendar cells can reverse a current or lag coefficient before outcomes are inspected.

sampling_model.design: A fixed-period observational panel is reweighted to the ex ante absorbing-path law \(\Pi\).
sampling_model.units: The triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) are independent and identically distributed draws from \(P\), with fixed \(T\).
sampling_model.treatment: The path \(W_i\) takes values in the declared absorbing support \(\mathcal S\).
sampling_model.overlap: The observed generalized propensity obeys \(\pi_s(X)\ge c_{\pi}\), and the reshaping law obeys \(\Pi_s\ge\epsilon\), for every \(s\in\mathcal S\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The core is a population identification and diagnostic result; estimation of \(\pi\) is not part of this specialization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under the known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

tldr: A reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is characterized as an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects. The loading tensor has both an ordered bridge-kernel formula and a pair-mass formula, its normalization reproduces the published homogeneous dynamic RIPW theorem, and rational inputs admit exact rank and contamination certificates. The unresolved theorem asks for an ordered adjacent-mass rule that classifies every loading sign and every zero off-diagonal entry without solving the exhausted inverse-image problem.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory states consistency of dynamic coefficients under effects that are homogeneous over calendar time and explicitly leaves the time-varying DATE equation beyond scope. Conventional event-study decompositions retain cohort and horizon cells but do not study counterfactual assignment-law reshaping with finite-memory lag regressors.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the forward coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag tensor under a fixed positive reshaping law, together with a support-only rank test and an ordered sign geometry.
project_justification.fill: The project derives that tensor in pair-mass and Green-kernel coordinates, certifies its exact computation, proves its strict reduction to the homogeneous theorem, and isolates the sign frontier as the open structural problem.

related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) supply the RIPW design, the DATE equation, and a dynamic consistency theorem under calendar-homogeneous lag effects; Theorem \(3\) makes their result an exact special case and proves strict extension beyond its maintained model. Sun and Abraham (2021) provide the foundational decomposition of conventional event-study coefficients into own-horizon and cross-horizon cohort effects; their residualization logic informs, but is not claimed to be tightened by, the reshaped lag-design tensor. Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) analyze carryover under known experimental assignment and motivate treatment-history indexing; their finite-population estimators are distinct from the present observational reshaping functional. De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) analyze complex treatment paths and a random-coefficient distributed-lag model whose effects remain constant over time; their result confirms that calendar variation remains outside the closest distributed-lag recovery framework. Wright (2026) gives conventional staggered-event-study probability-limit diagnostics and orthogonal scores but does not use assignment-law reshaping or a finite-memory calendar-by-lag tensor, so it is treated only as adjacent public-manuscript evidence. Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) provide published modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients but do not study causal panel reshaping or fixed-effect loading geometry.
honest_scope: The forward loading identities, normalization, homogeneous reduction, support-rank certificate, and exact rational diagnostic are theorem obligations. The ordered sign-and-zero rule is genuinely open and is not supplied by the assumptions. The project does not characterize the inverse image of all attainable tensors, optimize over reshaping laws, or claim double-robust inference. When \(p=0\), Theorem \(2\) reduces to the static DATE loading identity of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo; when effects are homogeneous over calendar time, Theorem \(3\) reduces to their published dynamic theorem.

literature_map: The chosen seed was deepened along four adjacent threads. Dynamic RIPW gives the direct anchor and explicitly leaves time-varying dynamic effects beyond scope. Heterogeneous event-study decompositions establish cross-horizon contamination but use conventional cohort-time designs. Panel experiments supply finite-memory causal contrasts under known sequential assignment rather than an observational reshaping functional. Recent distributed-lag and design-diagnostic manuscripts retain time-constant effects or conventional event-time weights. None of these sources supplies the ordered bridge formula, pair-mass forward tensor, and fixed-law sign frontier together.
